To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the river plumes off NW Iberian Peninsula are highly dynamic, and their dynamics are controlled by upwelling/downwellings and bathymetry.
the river plume fronts of the Galicia and north Portugal coasts are associated with the upwelling/downwellings and the bathymetry of the area.
the river plume front is a dynamic feature that can expand and contract, and that its location and structure depend on the local wind field.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the dynamics and structure of the river plumes in a region of the Iberian margin, where the river plume fronts play a significant role in the ecosystem dynamics.
the dynamics of the plume front, the role of upwelling, and the relationship between plume fronts, instabilities, and thermal gradients.
the dynamics of river plume formation and its relation to the oceanographic conditions on the continental shelf off the Galician and north Portuguese coast.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the position and structure of river plume frontal systems off NW Iberian shelf is controlled by the interaction of the river plumes with the local circulation, which depends on the regional bathymetry and the wind conditions.
the position of the river plumes is determined by the balance between the river plume buoyancy and the local upwelling/ downwelling conditions.
river plume fronts in the study area are not permanent and are not always visible in satellite imagery, but are rather transient and highly variable in space and time.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the river plume fronts off Galicia and north Portugal are not stationary features but rather are dynamic structures with a strong dependence on the local wind field and bathymetry.
the MLD gradient is a good physical indicator of the position of the river plumes and the AVHRR thermal gradients are good tracers of the plume dynamics.
the river plume fronts off the NW Iberian coast are a result of the interaction between local upwelling, relaxation of upwelling, and the dynamics and thermodynamics of the river plumes.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the MLD gradient between the plume waters and the adjacent ocean is a robust indicator of the maximum extent of the plume, and the thermal gradients observed in AVHRR imagery are related to the dynamics of the plume front.
the MLD is a good indicator of plume fronts and that the plume fronts are not stationary.

the river plume front in the area is a dynamic feature that responds to the local circulation and that the MLD gradient can provide information on the extension and structure of the plume and on the local upwelling conditions.
